sn22.95:1.1: Pali _ayujjhā_ is apparently the city known as Ayodhya in Sanskrit, believed to be the legendary seat of the Okkāka (Sanskrit _ikṣvāku_) dynasty from which hailed many leading royal lineages in ancient India, including the Buddha’s. Ayodhya is identified with Sāketa, which is however on the Sarabhū (Sanskrit _sarayu_) river, not the Ganges. Perhaps the text here is mistaken (compare [sn35.241:1.1]()).
sn22.95:1.2: This discourse establishes that it is not merely the supposed self that is empty and lacks a substantial core, but each of the five aggregates is in itself empty. The text does not go so far as to say that the aggregates do not exist, for each of the things compared do actually exist, they just appear as something other than they are. A lump of foam is perfectly real as a lump of foam, it is just not a solid mass.
sn22.95:5.1: There are multiple readings for _akukkuccakajāta_ in parallels of this passage. Regardless of the exact form, the root appears to be _kuñc_ (“skew”). The word applies to both a banana plant (as here) and a sal tree ([an4.196:4.2]()).
sn22.95:13.2: That _lāpinī_ appears directly following the death of the body suggests the sense “lament”, which is attested in Sanskrit.
